title: The Pour lettering
status: All 69 raised marking windows and both underside identities are recognizable in the reviewed native commanded envelopes; physical legibility is unrecorded

method.horizontal: Actual STL glyph sections above the backing face compared with positive native model roads buffered by half each road's emitted width; supports and backing-face deposition excluded
method.side: Actual STL glyph sections beyond the plain X face compared with projected native strand widths and nominal deposition-height slabs. Native single-precision height-comment noise is snapped to 0.00001 mm for adjacent-slab union. Rotated values are read along their facet tangent
method.recessed: Actual P STL glyph voids below the first nozzle plane compared with positive native strand-width footprints on both open recess layers, viewed from the physical underside
method.coverage: Fraction of source glyph area covered by the union of commanded envelopes. Component fractions follow glyph source components in reading order; spaces are excluded
method.manual: Every exact ID, number, decimal point, axis convention and version/date string was inspected in the buffered overlays. Recognition, rather than outline perfection, is the criterion

limits: Commanded envelopes and nominal slabs are toolpath interpretation, not measured deposited dimensions or physical legibility
Small 4-diagonal notches and rounded corners remain recognizable in essential values; narrow side-angle details also show stair steps and some open strokes
Fine side-angle numerals retain number recognition; complete stroke connectivity is not claimed for those detail markings
Native archives and inspection images are local preparation evidence. Exact archive/G-code hashes identify that evidence independently of the editable projects
No printer submission, physical contrast, support cleanup or handling result is claimed
